draft.title: The Kokoda Track
card: The Kokoda Track is a narrow path over the Owen Stanley Range in Papua, then an Australian territory. The terrain was steep, muddy and covered in thick jungle.
In July 1942 Japanese forces landed on the north coast of Papua and advanced along the track. Their aim was to take Port Moresby, the main Australian base in the territory.
Australian soldiers fought the Japanese along the track for months. Papuan carriers helped them by carrying supplies and by carrying wounded soldiers out.
By late 1942 the Australians had pushed the Japanese back and Port Moresby did not fall. Many soldiers on both sides also suffered from disease and exhaustion.
draft.remember: On the Kokoda Track, Australians and Papuan carriers stopped the Japanese advance on Port Moresby.

a.q: Why did Japanese forces advance along the Kokoda Track in 1942?
opts: To capture Port Moresby, the Australian base in Papua
To capture Darwin, on the northern coast of Australia
To free Australian prisoners held in northern Papua
To cut off Australian troops fighting in Libya
a.why: The Japanese were trying to cross the range to take Port Moresby, the main Australian base in Papua. Darwin was bombed from the air and was not the aim of the track campaign, which is a common mix-up.
a.clue: Think about where the track leads on the far side of the mountains.

b.q: During the Kokoda campaign, what did Papuan carriers do to help Australian soldiers?
opts: Carried supplies in and wounded soldiers out
Led the Australian attack on Port Moresby
Took over the defence of the track alone
Carried the Japanese prisoners to the coast
b.why: Papuan carriers moved food, ammunition and other supplies along the steep track and carried wounded soldiers out. They did not replace the soldiers in the fighting. The track was the route for the Japanese advance, so there was no attack on Port Moresby to lead.
b.clue: Think about how supplies could reach soldiers in steep jungle.

a.best: To capture Port Moresby, the Australian base in Papua

b.best: Carried supplies in and wounded soldiers out
